concepts.label: te-node
concepts.gloss: A TE node is a network element represented as a vertex within a particular traffic-engineering topology and serving as the attachment point for TE termination and switching resources.
concepts.example: R2 is a TE node in the OTN-layer topology, with termination points for the R1–R2 and R2–R3 TE links and a node-local connectivity matrix.

concepts.label: termination-point
concepts.gloss: A termination point is a node-local TE interface at which a TE link terminates, identifying the link-facing endpoint on that node.
concepts.example: tp-R1-R2 is the termination point on R1 that terminates telink-R1-R2 at its R1 end.

concepts.label: supporting-tp
concepts.gloss: A supporting termination point records the lower-layer termination resource that carries or adapts a higher-layer termination point.
concepts.example: At R1, an optical-layer termination point is the supporting TP for an OTN-layer termination point carried over it.
instances: OTN tp over optical tp at R1
ODU tp over OTU tp at R2

concepts.label: tunnel-termination-point
concepts.gloss: A tunnel termination point is a node-local service endpoint from which a TE tunnel originates, as distinct from a physical or layer-link termination point.
concepts.example: ttp-A1 is the tunnel head on node A1 from which tunnel-a1a3-odu2 originates toward A3.

concepts.label: te-tunnel
concepts.gloss: A TE tunnel is an engineered connectivity service originating at a tunnel termination point, routed over a TE topology, and optionally associated with a protection group.
concepts.example: tunnel-a1a3-odu2 is a protected ODU2 tunnel originating at A1, crossing the relevant TE topology to A3, and protected by pgroup-a1a3.

concepts.label: otn-label
concepts.gloss: An OTN label is the tributary-slot and, where applicable, tributary-port-number allocation that identifies how a tunnel's ODU signal is multiplexed into a containing OTN signal.
concepts.example: For an ODU2 tunnel carried in an OTU4, the OTN label specifies the TS/TPN resources allocated to that ODU2 within the OTU4.

concepts.label: connectivity-matrix
concepts.gloss: A connectivity matrix is a node-local switching model that states which termination points or connection endpoints can be internally connected by that TE node.
concepts.example: The R2 connectivity matrix permits traffic arriving on the R1-facing termination point to be switched to the R3-facing termination point.

concepts.label: te-link
concepts.gloss: A TE link is a traffic-engineering adjacency between TE nodes whose ends are represented by termination points on those nodes.
concepts.example: telink-R1-R2 connects nodes R1 and R2 and is terminated by an R1-side TP and an R2-side TP.

concepts.label: te-topology
concepts.gloss: A TE topology is a layer-specific network view containing the TE nodes and TE links over which paths and tunnels at that layer are engineered.
concepts.example: The OTN layer network is a TE topology containing OTN-visible nodes such as R1 and R2 and their OTN TE links.

concepts.label: tunnel-connection-endpoint
concepts.gloss: A tunnel connection endpoint is a node-local endpoint belonging to a specific tunnel that marks where that tunnel's connection is instantiated, entered, exited, or cross-connected at the node.
concepts.example: tcep-a1a3-R1 is the R1-local connection endpoint belonging to the A1–A3 tunnel, while tcep-a1a3-R3 represents that tunnel connection at R3.

concepts.label: wson-optical-channel
concepts.gloss: A WSON optical channel is an individually identifiable wavelength or frequency-slot connection carried over one or more optical multiplex sections.
concepts.example: och-lambda1-R1-R3 is the optical channel using lambda1 between R1 and R3 over the applicable OMS resources.

concepts.label: optical-multiplex-section
concepts.gloss: An optical multiplex section is a link-like optical span between nodes that aggregates and transports multiple optical channels as a wavelength-division-multiplexed group.
concepts.example: oms-R1-R2 is the optical multiplex section between R1 and R2 and can aggregate och-lambda1 together with other optical channels on that span.

concepts.label: service-grade
concepts.gloss: A service grade is the service-tier classification assigned to a TE tunnel to express its relative service treatment or policy class independently of its route and signal type.
concepts.example: tunnel-a1a3-odu2 is assigned the gold service grade, whereas tunnel-a2a3-odu0 is assigned silver.

concepts.label: protection-group
concepts.gloss: A protection group is a protection construct associated with a tunnel that groups alternative resources or paths and assigns them working and protection roles, such as in a 1+1 scheme.
concepts.example: pgroup-a1a3 protects tunnel-a1a3-odu2 using a 1+1 arrangement containing one working path and one protect path.

concepts.label: protection-role
concepts.gloss: A protection role identifies the function of a member path or resource within a protection group, principally whether it is the normal working member or the standby/protect member.
concepts.example: Within pgroup-a1a3, R1–R3 has the working role and R1–R4–R3 has the protect role.

concepts.label: ext-tlv-42
concepts.gloss: ext-tlv-42 is an opaque node-level extension attribute whose type code and uninterpreted payload preserve implementation-specific TE information not otherwise modeled by the schema.
concepts.example: R2 carries ext-tlv-42 with the opaque value 0x77, which a system retains or forwards without inferring additional semantics from the value.
